event: Nala draws the bolt and opens the door; Shaestrel stands in the sun with a warm loaf.
She comes in, breaks the loaf on the cutting table and hands Nala the heel.
Nala eats standing and gets to work, tacking the bodice pieces together.
Shaestrel watches a while, then says she'll come back at lamp-lighting for the silk.
She leaves by the door, as a mortal would, in the full sun.
All day Nala sews: bodice, sleeves, the long skirt panels joined at the waist.
By evening the gown hangs whole on the back-room door, its hem left to set.

changes.note: Silk sewn into the gown; only the hem left to set
changes.from: Grey-green silk cut into the pieces of the gown, with an arm's length left over.
changes.to: A grey-green silk gown sewn whole but for its pinned hem, with an arm's length of silk left over.

event: Nala lights the lamps as the light turns gold and low.
Shaestrel knocks and comes in, and stops when she sees the gown.
